newsitem.title: USA: US Treasuries open higher, 30-yr yield 6.49 pct.
newsitem.headline: US Treasuries open higher, 30-yr yield 6.49 pct.

text.p: U.S. Treasury prices opened higher on Tuesday, the first trading session of the week in New York after the bond markets closed for Veterans Day on Monday.
"Prices rebounded in Asia and climbed a bit further in London trade," said Kim Rupert, economist at MMS International.
Rupert said the market retains a bullish tone and that economic data on October due later this week was unlikely to disrupt that positive feeling.
At 0800 EST/1300 GMT, the 6-1/2-percent 30-year benchmark Treasury bond was up 6/32 to 100-3/32 to yield 6.49 percent.

Inflation data on wholesale and consumer prices due this week should be bond-friendly, economists say. The October Producer Price Index (PPI), due Wednesday, is expected to be up a modest 0.2 percent after a 0.2 percent September increase. Without its food and energy items, the PPI is expected to be up an ever-so-slight 0.1 percent after a 0.3 percent blip up in September.

The October Consumer Price Index (CPI), due a day later, is expected to be up 0.3 percent, matching September's gain. Without its food and energy components, the CPI is expected to be up 0.2 percent, compared with September's 0.3 percent rise.

Retail sales data for October, due on Thursday, are also expected to be benign in terms of the bond market's concerns. Economists polled by Reuters estimated, on average, that sales rose only 0.3 percent in October after a 0.7 percent September gain. Retail sales have been lackluster for months. In the context of strong job and personal income growth, that has led many economists to expect a sales rebound in the last two months of the fourth quarter.
The only fresh data that the market gets today is the survey of local business conditions in the area of the Richmond (Virginia) Federal Reserve.

The Richmond Fed report includes indices on the manufacturing and service sectors of the economy. In the September report, both the the Richmond Fed's shipments index and its services index had readings of -2.0.

The Treasury will sell $28.0 billion in three- and six-month bills at 1300 EST/1800 GMT at its weekly bill auction, postponed by a day due to the Veterans Day holiday. The bidding deadline for the auction is 1300 EST/1800 GMT.
In early trade, three- and six-month bill rates were down one and two basis points, respectively, to 5.02 percent and 5.08 percent.
Year bill rates were down two basis points to 6.15 percent.
Two-year notes were up 2/32 to 100-9/32 to yield 5.72 pct. Five-year notes rose 3/32 to 101 even to yield 6.01 percent.
Ten-year notes were up 6/32 to 101-31, yielding 6.23 percent.
The 6-1/2 percent 30-year yield of 6.49 percent is the lowest for the benchmark bond since the March 7 close of 6.46 percent.
